proof.criterion: Architect's addition (b): recordedMarkRefs uses the anchor indexes and returns the same rows
proof.surface: warmed replay database (Postgres 17, 14,887 comments) and go test ./internal/dispatch/docs/
proof.command: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) of both queries prepared with a text parameter, generic plan, artifact 0a8f575b-…; set comparison of old vs new predicates over all 1,157 artifacts; go test -run 'RecordedMark|TestSettle|TestMarkOnlyUpdateSweeps'
proof.observed: comments Seq Scan 11.77 ms (14,869 rows removed) -> Bitmap Index Scan on comments_anchor_artifact 0.16 ms, same 18 rows; asks Seq Scan 0.14 ms -> index scan on asks_anchor_artifact 0.09 ms; old vs new rows: comments 3,400 = 3,400, symmetric difference 0; TestRecordedMarkRefsListsOnlyTheDocumentsAnchoredRows passes; sweep tests pass unchanged
proof.negativeControl: comments artifact filter dropped: the new test fails with proofComment …b1 (anchored on another document) in the set

trickyParts: Walk vs walk: identical lists because walkNode skips only children of text and leaf nodes, which Validate refuses to carry; every tree sweepUnrecordedMarks gets comes through pmdoc.Read/ReadInTransaction or ParseFragment.

recordedMarkRefs keeps the text comparison beside the index expression so the rows are exactly the old rows (a uuid compare alone would also match a case-different artifact_id). The asks coalesce equals the anchor's artifact_id because only the ask-block insert sets block_artifact_id and it writes no anchor; no constraint enforces that, only the code.
